title: SHAP explainer logging: the nested scikit-learn model is serialized with cloudpickle, not skops, because the explainer itself is already pickle
answers: Why does logging a SHAP explainer for a scikit-learn tree model fail with an untrusted type error from skops?
Which serialization format does mlflow.shap.log_explainer use for the underlying sklearn model?
Where is the SHAP explainer save path that extracts and saves the inner sklearn model?
Does saving a standalone sklearn model with mlflow.sklearn change when SHAP is involved?
body:
Path: mlflow.shap.log_explainer and mlflow.shap.save_explainer (chokepoint mlflow/shap/__init__.py:save_explainer) handle logging or saving a SHAP explainer with serialize_model_using_mlflow=True. When the wrapped model is sklearn, the inner estimator is extracted and saved as an MLmodel sub-artifact under underlying_model.
Rule: save_explainer passes serialization_format=mlflow.sklearn.SERIALIZATION_FORMAT_CLOUDPICKLE to mlflow.sklearn.save_model for that nested model. Do not auto-trust skops types for it (for example sklearn.tree._tree.Tree) and do not add a trust-list option to this path, because the SHAP artifact is already pickle-based and the nested model shares that trust boundary. Standalone mlflow.sklearn saves keep skops as default.
Symptom: Logging a SHAP explainer over a scikit-learn tree model failed because skops 0.15 rejects sklearn.tree._tree.Tree by default, unless the caller supplied a trusted-types list.
Constraints: Applies only to the sklearn branch of save_explainer. The pytorch branch and standalone mlflow.sklearn.log_model/save_model are unaffected. Test coverage: tests/shap/test_log.py:test_log_model_serializes_underlying_model_with_cloudpickle asserts the format is cloudpickle, skops_trusted_types is None, and model.pkl exists.
applies: Use when touching how MLflow SHAP explainers save or log their nested scikit-learn model, or when a SHAP logging call fails on skops untrusted types.
says: Logging model explanations for a tree-based model fails with an untrusted type error.
Saving an explainer for a machine learning model crashes due to security type checks.
Packaging model explainability artifacts should not require configuring trusted types manually.
Recording feature importance explainers alongside trained models fails during the save process.
Allow logging explainers without triggering security rejections on the underlying model.
search: When logging or saving SHAP explainers with serialize_model_using_mlflow=True, mlflow/shap/__init__.py:save_explainer forces serialization_format=mlflow.sklearn.SERIALIZATION_FORMAT_CLOUDPICKLE when saving the nested scikit-learn underlying_model. Cloudpickle is used instead of skops because the outer SHAP explainer is already pickle-based, so no skops_trusted_types list is accepted or auto-configured on this path. This rule applies strictly to the sklearn branch of save_explainer to fix untrusted type errors on sklearn.tree._tree.Tree, leaving standalone mlflow.sklearn saves and the pytorch branch unaffected.
